property_summary: After a call to play(), pot should be either the balance sent with the call or zero, never negative.
After a play() call, pot should be greater than or equal to the amount sent minus the fee if the player wins.
After each play() call, the pot must be either zero (if the player wins) or equal to the total amount sent by all losing players (i.e., the accumulated ticket amounts from non-winning calls).

After each play() call, the pot is equal to the ticket amount (10) minus the fee (1) only when the player wins, otherwise it should be the accumulated ticket amount from all losing plays; the bug breaks this by always resetting pot to 0 regardless of the game outcome.

After each play() call, pot should be either the accumulated ticket amount (if player lost) or exactly the ticket amount minus the fee (if player won), never zero when player loses and the pot was non-zero before.
After each play call, pot is either 0 or exactly the amount that would remain after adding the fee (i.e., pot == 9) in case of a win, and pot is unchanged in case of a loss.
After any sequence of play() calls, the pot equals the number of wins times (TICKET_AMOUNT - FEE_AMOUNT).
After each play() call, the final pot is always less than 2 * TICKET_AMOUNT.
After any play() call, the pot is a multiple of (TICKET_AMOUNT - FEE_AMOUNT) plus any leftover from a previous win.
After any play() call, the pot is either 0 (if random != 0) or the sum of the pot before the call plus TICKET_AMOUNT minus FEE_AMOUNT (if random == 0), which is invariant under the bug.
After any sequence of public calls, calling play() should reset pot to 0 when random == 0.
After a win (random == 0) via play(), the pot state variable should be 0.
After a call to play(), pot is always at most the total value sent in that call minus the fee taken, i.e., pot never exceeds the total value sent in the last call minus 1.
After any call to play() that results in a win (random == 0), the total bank balance must equal its initial balance plus one fee for each win so far.
After any call to play(), the pot is either zero (if the player won) or the sum of all tickets sent in that call (if the player lost).
After a play() call that results in a win (random == 0), the pot state variable should be zero.
After a winning play() call (random == 0), the pot is set to zero only if the bank received the fee.
After a winning play() call (random == 0), the total amount transferred to the bank and the player equals TICKET_AMOUNT (the amount paid by the player).
After any call to play(), the pot state variable is always either 0 or TICKET_AMOUNT.
After a winning play() call (random == 0), the total amount transferred to bank and player equals TICKET_AMOUNT.

After calling play(), either the pot is zero (winner case) or the pot equals the sent amount (no winner case); the reference always transitions pot to zero or keeps it exactly msg.value, while the mutant can leak fee even when nobody wins.
The pot is always zero after a play() call that does not revert.

After an unreverted play() call, the pot must be zero only if random was 0, but with the bug the pot is nonzero when random equals 1 or 2. The rule: after a successful play(), the pot is always 0 (since the correct contract always pays out when random==0 and leaves pot=0; buggy contract may leave pot unchanged when random !=0).
After a successful play() call, the pot is always 0.

After a successful play() call, the sender's balance increases by exactly 10 (the ticket amount) minus 1 (the fee) when the random value computed modulo 2 is 0, but with the bug using modulo 3 the condition changes.

After any play() call that does not revert, the pot must be equal to the sum of all msg.value sent minus any payouts made, but the bug causes the pot to remain unchanged when random != 0 (mod 3) while reference pays out only when random == 0 (mod 2).
